note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a PAK 9, 14, 1926 Act 3, 7; A06b PAK 9, 14, 1926 Act 3, 8; L05 PAK 14): ordinary naturalisation after 5 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships (with major exceptions); a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another (with exceptions). Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Pakistan, 2024
sources.said: Person has been resident in Pakistan for 12 months immediately prior to the application, as well as during 4 out of 7 years predating the 12-month period. ... Renunciation of citizenship of another country required. Dual citizenship allowed with the United Kingdom and any other country that the Federal Government may specify ... The person acquiring a foreign citizenship (or is about to acquire) may relinquish Pakistan citizenship voluntarily, asking the government to release him. When Pakistan citizenship is not relinquished voluntarily in this situation, it lapses ipso facto. Provision does not apply to a female citizen of Pakistan who is married to a person who is not a citizen of Pakistan. Provision is not applied to persons who acquire citizenship in the following countries: UK, France, Italy, Belgium, Iceland, Australia, New Zealand, Canada, Finland, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Switzerland, the Netherlands, USA, Sweden, Ireland, Bahrain and Denmark.
